text: Google once tried to sell itself for under a million dollars. The buyer said no.
In 1999, Google was a tiny startup run by two Stanford students, Larry Page and Sergey Brin.
say: In nineteen ninety-nine, Google was a tiny startup run by two Stanford students, Larry Page and Sergey Brin.

text: They offered it to Excite, one of the biggest search websites back then.
An Excite investor even talked it down to $750,000.
say: An Excite investor even talked it down to seven hundred and fifty thousand.

text: Why? Reportedly, Google was too good.
It found your answer so fast that people left the site straight away.
And Excite made its money from ads, so it wanted visitors to stay and click around.
Today, Google is worth trillions. And Excite? Most people have never heard of it.
The lesson for your website? Don't make people hunt for what they need.
Get them the answer fast, and they'll come back.
